en: Non-being was not, nor was being then; there was no airy space, nor the sky which is beyond.
What stirred? Where? In whose shelter? Was there water, deep, unfathomable? 1
Death was not, nor deathlessness then; there was no sign of night or of day.
That One breathed, windless, by its own power; other than that there was nothing at all beyond. 2
Darkness there was, hidden by darkness, in the beginning; all this was water without a sign.
What was coming to be, covered by emptiness, that One was born by the power of heat. 3
Desire came upon it in the beginning, which was the first seed of mind.
The poets, searching in the heart with insight, found the bond of being in non-being. 4
Their cord was stretched across: was there a below? was there an above?
There were seed-placers, there were powers; own-power below, giving forth above. 5
Who truly knows? Who shall declare it here: from where it was born, from where this creation?
The gods are later than the creation of this; then who knows from where it came into being? 6
This creation, from where it came into being, whether it was set in place or whether not —
he who is its overseer in the highest heaven, he surely knows; or perhaps he does not know. 7
rom: nāsad āsīn no sad āsīt tadānīṃ nāsīd rajo no vyomā paro yat |
kim āvarīvaḥ kuha kasya śarmann ambhaḥ kim āsīd gahanaṃ gabhīram || 1 ||
na mṛtyur āsīd amṛtaṃ na tarhi na rātryā ahna āsīt praketaḥ |
ānīd avātaṃ svadhayā tad ekaṃ tasmād dhānyan na paraḥ kiṃ canāsa || 2 ||
tama āsīt tamasā gūḷham agre 'praketaṃ salilaṃ sarvam ā idam |
tucchyenābhv apihitaṃ yad āsīt tapasas tan mahinājāyataikam || 3 ||
kāmas tad agre sam avartatādhi manaso retaḥ prathamaṃ yad āsīt |
sato bandhum asati nir avindan hṛdi pratīṣyā kavayo manīṣā || 4 ||
tiraścīno vitato raśmir eṣām adhaḥ svid āsī3d upari svid āsī3t |
retodhā āsan mahimāna āsant svadhā avastāt prayatiḥ parastāt || 5 ||
ko addhā veda ka iha pra vocat kuta ājātā kuta iyaṃ visṛṣṭiḥ |
arvāg devā asya visarjanenāthā ko veda yata ābabhūva || 6 ||
iyaṃ visṛṣṭir yata ābabhūva yadi vā dadhe yadi vā na |
yo asyādhyakṣaḥ parame vyomant so aṅga veda yadi vā na veda || 7 ||
notes: Each stanza is one verse in two half-lines; the original's verse numbers are kept at the end of the second half-line.
1.1: 'rajas' here is the middle region, the airy space between earth and sky.
1.2: 'āvarīvaḥ' is disputed: 'what covered (it)?' or 'what stirred / moved to and fro?'.
3.2: 'ābhu' is disputed: 'what was coming into being', 'the void', 'the potential'; 'tapas' is heat, also ascetic fervour.
5.1: 'āsī3t' carries the pluti (a prolonged vowel, the numeral 3 in the original), marking a question; 'raśmi' is a cord or ray.
7.1: 'dadhe' may be 'he/it established (it)' or 'it was established': whether it was made or not.
